title: The Sun's Nearest Neighbours
subtitle: A survey traverse of every star within ~12.5 light-years
intro: Charted like Darwin's Beagle working its way along a coastline, this voyage steps outward from the Sun through the local stellar neighbourhood, one system at a time, in order of true distance. Most of these neighbours are dim red dwarfs invisible to the naked eye — the real demographics of our galaxy.

waypoints.title: Sol — home port
waypoints.narrative: Departure point. A middle-aged G2V dwarf; every distance on this map is measured from here.
waypoints.name: Sol

waypoints.title: Proxima Centauri
waypoints.narrative: The single closest star to the Sun, an M5.5 red dwarf so faint it was only found in 1915. It hosts Proxima b, a roughly Earth-mass planet in its habitable zone.
waypoints.name: Proxima Centauri

waypoints.title: Rigil Kentaurus (Alpha Centauri A)
waypoints.narrative: The brighter member of the Alpha Centauri triple system and a near-twin of our own Sun. To the unaided eye it and Toliman merge into the third-brightest star in the night sky.
waypoints.name: Rigil Kentaurus

waypoints.title: Barnard's Star
waypoints.narrative: A red dwarf with the largest proper motion of any star — it slides a full lunar diameter across the sky every 180 years. A "runaway star" racing through the solar neighbourhood.
waypoints.name: Barnard's Star

waypoints.title: Wolf 359
waypoints.narrative: A tiny, flaring M6 dwarf, one of the lowest-mass and faintest stars known. Famous to a generation as the site of a fictional battle, it is very real and very close.
waypoints.name: Wolf 359

waypoints.title: Lalande 21185
waypoints.narrative: The brightest red dwarf in the northern sky, yet still far too faint to see without a telescope. Long-term astrometry hints at a family of planets.
waypoints.name: Lalande 21185

waypoints.title: Sirius
waypoints.narrative: The brightest star in Earth’s night sky, a hot A-type star orbited by Sirius B, a dense white-dwarf ember — the burnt-out core of a once more massive companion.
waypoints.name: Sirius

waypoints.title: Ross 154
waypoints.narrative: A young, magnetically active red dwarf in Sagittarius that erupts in powerful flares, brightening in minutes.
waypoints.name: Ross 154

waypoints.title: Ross 248
waypoints.narrative: A flare star drifting toward us; in roughly 36,000 years it will briefly become the closest star to the Sun, before Proxima reclaims the title.
waypoints.name: Ross 248

waypoints.title: Epsilon Eridani (Ran)
waypoints.narrative: A young orange dwarf ringed by dusty debris belts and at least one giant planet — a solar system caught in the act of forming.
waypoints.name: Ran

waypoints.title: Lacaille 9352
waypoints.narrative: A red dwarf in Piscis Austrinus with two known planets and the fourth-largest proper motion of any star.
waypoints.name: Lacaille 9352

waypoints.title: Ross 128
waypoints.narrative: A quiet, old red dwarf hosting Ross 128 b, a temperate Earth-mass world — one of the nearest exoplanets that could plausibly be clement.
waypoints.name: Ross 128

waypoints.title: 61 Cygni
waypoints.narrative: The "Flying Star" — in 1838 the first star to have its distance measured by parallax, a keystone of the cosmic distance ladder. A wide pair of orange dwarfs.
waypoints.name: 61 Cyg

waypoints.title: Procyon
waypoints.narrative: The eighth-brightest star in the sky, a bright F-type star with its own white-dwarf companion, Procyon B.
waypoints.name: Procyon

waypoints.title: Tau Ceti
waypoints.narrative: The nearest lone Sun-like star, long a touchstone of the search for other Earths. It carries a massive debris disk and several candidate planets.
waypoints.name: 52Tau Cet

waypoints.title: Epsilon Indi
waypoints.narrative: An orange dwarf accompanied by a pair of cool brown dwarfs — failed stars — and a confirmed giant planet.
waypoints.name: Eps Ind

title: Voyager — the Interstellar Errand
subtitle: Where our farthest machines are actually heading
intro: Humanity's first interstellar craft carry no engines that matter now — they coast forever on the momentum of planetary slingshots. This voyage plots the real stars the Voyager and Pioneer probes will drift past across the next million years, each encounter tens of thousands of years away.

waypoints.title: Sol — launch, 1972–1977
waypoints.narrative: Pioneer 10 & 11 and Voyager 1 & 2 all began here, flung outward by gravity assists off the giant planets onto escape trajectories out of the Solar System.
waypoints.name: Sol

waypoints.title: Voyager 1 → Gliese 445
waypoints.narrative: Voyager 1, the most distant human object, is climbing north out of the galactic plane. In about 40,000 years it will pass within ~1.6 light-years of Gliese 445, a faint red dwarf now in Camelopardalis.
waypoints.name: Voyager 1 → Gliese 445

waypoints.title: Voyager 2 → Ross 248
waypoints.narrative: In roughly 40,000 years Voyager 2 will drift within ~1.7 light-years of Ross 248 — which, by then, will itself be the closest star to the Sun.
waypoints.name: Ross 248

waypoints.title: Voyager 2 → Sirius
waypoints.narrative: Far deeper into the future — some 296,000 years from now — Voyager 2 will glide about 4.3 light-years past Sirius, the brightest star in our sky.
waypoints.name: Sirius

waypoints.title: Pioneer 10 → Aldebaran
waypoints.narrative: Pioneer 10, silent since 2003, is aimed toward Aldebaran, the red-giant eye of Taurus. At its coasting speed the crossing would take over two million years.
waypoints.name: Aldebaran

title: An Interstellar Odyssey
subtitle: A mythic grand tour that mirrors Homer
intro: Ulysses' voyage home from Troy is the archetypal story-voyage: a route of trials traced across a map. Here the same shape is laid over the brightest beacons of the night sky — depart Ithaca, endure the wonders and terrors of the deep, and return. Every star and its physics are real; only the myth is borrowed.

waypoints.title: Ithaca — the Sun
waypoints.narrative: The harbour we leave and long to regain. From this ordinary yellow dwarf every heading is measured, and to it the whole voyage bends back.
waypoints.name: Sol

waypoints.title: Sirius — the beacon set alight
waypoints.narrative: We cast off toward the sky’s brightest star, the Dog Star that the ancients watched rise with the summer heat. Its blue-white glare is the lighthouse at the mouth of the dark sea.
waypoints.name: Sirius

waypoints.title: Aldebaran — the eye of the Cyclops
waypoints.narrative: A single vast red eye glares from the Hyades: Aldebaran, a bloated orange giant forty times the Sun’s girth. We slip past its stare and press on into open sky.
waypoints.name: Aldebaran

waypoints.title: Rigel — the bag of winds
waypoints.narrative: At Orion’s foot burns Rigel, a blue supergiant pouring out a hundred thousand times the Sun’s light. Here the winds are loosed — a star so luminous its radiation storms across light-years.
waypoints.name: Rigel

waypoints.title: Betelgeuse — the house of the dead
waypoints.narrative: A doomed red supergiant, so swollen it would swallow Jupiter’s orbit, flickering toward the supernova that will end it. We pass through the shadow of a star already dying, the land of the shades.
waypoints.name: Betelgeuse

waypoints.title: Antares — Scylla and Charybdis
waypoints.narrative: The red heart of the Scorpion, a supergiant rival to Mars, marks the strait of monsters. We thread between its churning stellar wind and the crush of its gravity, and survive.
waypoints.name: Antares

waypoints.title: Vega — the song of the Sirens
waypoints.narrative: Brilliant, swift-spinning Vega was once the pole star and will be again. Its clear blue song has lured astronomers for two centuries; ringed by a disk of debris, it nearly holds us fast.
waypoints.name: Vega

waypoints.title: Altair — the swift crossing
waypoints.narrative: The Eagle’s star spins so fast — a full rotation in nine hours — that it bulges at its equator. On its rushing winds we make the swift passage of the Summer Triangle.
waypoints.name: Altair

waypoints.title: Deneb — Calypso's far island
waypoints.narrative: Farthest of all our ports, Deneb blazes as one of the most luminous stars known, yet hangs so remote its distance is still argued. Here, at the edge of the map, the voyage lingers longest before turning for home.
waypoints.name: Deneb

waypoints.title: Arcturus — the Bear-guard points home
waypoints.narrative: The old orange giant "Guardian of the Bear" wheels near the celestial pole and has steered navigators for millennia. By its light we set the final heading back toward Ithaca.
waypoints.name: Arcturus

waypoints.title: Ithaca regained — the Sun
waypoints.narrative: The long arc closes. We fall back toward the pale yellow star we set out from, the voyage told and the map complete.
waypoints.name: Sol
